title.narrative: NIHR HSPR-CA - Social participation for universal health coverage: evidence-informed networks advancing inclusion

description.narrative: The project has 5 objectives: 1. To align, strengthen, evaluate, and sustain intra-and inter -country academic and civil society partnerships working on social participation of transgender populations for universal health coverage (UHC) with a specific emphasis on the “leave no one behind” agenda in Vietnam, India, and Thailand.​ 2. To understand the contexts, mechanisms, outcomes, and costs of involving transgender populations in social participation for health initiatives as well as social participation (of any group) in UHC reform initiatives at national and subnational levels in each country.​ 3. To co-produce country-specific as well as cross-country mechanisms intended to enhance meaningful inclusion of transgender populations in social participation for health geared towards achieving UHC.​ 4. To evaluate and or assess the relationship of these mechanisms to health system process goals from the perspective of community, civil society, government, and academic actors.​ 5. To catalyse exchange and expansion of the social participation for universal health coverage - evidence-informed networks advancing inclusion (SUNWAI) in the run-up to the endpoint of the sustainable development goals in 2030 and beyond​.

The social participation for universal health coverage - evidence-informed networks advancing inclusion (SUNWAI) consortium seeks to institutionalise and deepen cross-regional research and action that advances the inclusion of key populations – specifically transgender communities in social participation for universal health coverage (UHC), and to understand its contexts, mechanisms, outcomes, and costs. The study will build within and cross-country partnerships between community (especially key populations), civil society, government and academic actors to understand the context of social participation for UHC, the mechanisms used, what these cost and what kinds of outcomes they yield. The study will also have a participatory action research (PAR) component, whereby it will promote mechanisms to improve inclusion of key populations in social participation for UHC.
The study will be undertaken by Hanoi Medical University Vietnam, The George Institute for Global Health India, Mahidol University Thailand, and University of Essex England. The project will conduct 6 studies in Thailand, Vietnam and India between June 2025 and May 2030.
Achievement of UHC, like other sustainable development goals (SDGs) targets, means that we “leave no one behind.” There is global recognition that this requires actual social participation of people affected by UHC policies. In Asia, sexual and gender minorities - that is transgender persons or men who have sex with men - have had variable involvement with health priority-setting: flagship UHC reforms, mostly related to insurance, rarely involves them. SUNWAI (Hindu/Urdu for “being heard”) is a consortium that will use participatory and realist research methods to enhance the inclusion of sexual and gender minorities (SGM) in UHC-related social participation platforms. In Vietnam, Thailand and India, it has taken approximately four decades for sexual and gender minorities to be recognised and granted entitlements, with potential for access to health under UHC reform. Yet, there are still gaps on what the role of SGM can be in UHC reform, what the related contexts, mechanisms, costs and outcomes could be.
